title: Stochastic backoff heatmap scratch (Inga)
content:
Goal:
Quick exploration of stochastic backoff parameters vs observed tail latency under bursty ingress. Trying to map regimes where small randomized backoff reduces p99 without killing throughput.

Motivation / context:
- We see occasional microbursts where p99 spikes 2-3x for a few seconds then recovers. Suspect synchronized retry/backoff interactions in our frontend proxies + request fanout into GPU workers.
- Idea: instead of fixed exponential backoff, use a tiny randomized multiplicative jitter at the admission/proxy level and tune factor distribution. Want a cheap signal (no stateful queues) that smooths spikes.

Experiment sketch (local sim + small cluster run):
1) Workloads: baseline Poisson arrival (lambda=200 rps), and bursty (sinusoidal envelope with amplitude 0.6, period 30s) plus a few launched microburst events (500ms at 2k rps). Payload: 150-token generation, same model variant.
2) Backoff variants:
   A) none (immediate retries up to 3 attempts)
   B) fixed exponential (base=50ms, max=800ms)
   C) stochastic multiplicative: base * U(0.6,1.4) applied each retry
   D) log-normal jitter: base * exp(N(0, sigma^2)) with sigma=0.25
   E) capped-randomized-window: uniform(20ms..window) with window tuned
3) Metrics: p50/p95/p99 latency, success rate, tail throughput (tokens/s), retry count per request, short-term latency variance (10s window). Capture full traces for a subset.
4) Sweep dims: backoff base {30,50,100} ms and jitter scale(s) where applicable. Run 10x reps per cell (60s warmup + 180s run).

Representative run summary (bursty workload, base=50ms):
- None: p50=120ms, p95=420ms, p99=1120ms, success=99.2%, retries avg=1.8, tokens/s drop 7% during microburst
- Fixed exp: p50=125ms, p95=360ms, p99=820ms, success=99.6%, retries avg=1.6, tokens/s steady (less drop)
- Stochastic mult (U(0.6,1.4)): p50=130ms, p95=320ms, p99=540ms, success=99.7%, retries avg=1.4, tokens/s steady +2%
- Log-normal (sigma=0.25): p50=128ms, p95=330ms, p99=580ms, success=99.6%, retries avg=1.45
- Capped window (20..200ms): p50=135ms, p95=350ms, p99=670ms, success=99.5%

Quick ASCII heatmap (p99 ms) rows=backoff base (30/50/100), cols=variant (none,exp,stoch,logn,cap):
base=30ms: [none:980, exp:720, stoch:460, logn:500, cap:600]
base=50ms: [none:1120, exp:820, stoch:540, logn:580, cap:670]
base=100ms:[none:1350, exp:930, stoch:620, logn:660, cap:750]

Observations / interpretations:
- The stochastic multiplicative jitter consistently reduces p99 more than deterministic exponential backoff across base values. Effect strongest at lower base (30-50ms).
- Increasing base delays shifts the tail right (longer p99) for 'none' and fixed exp, but stochastic jitter absorbs synchronization by spreading retries temporally.
- Log-normal with small sigma performs close to uniform multiplicative jitter; it's slightly more conservative (heavier mean) because exp(N) skews >1 occasionally.
- Capped uniform windows help but are sensitive to cap size; too-large caps hurt p50 and throughput during steady-state.
- Success rate improves slightly with jitter; retries per request drop — an indicator we avoided clumping.

Telemetry notes / what to capture next time:
- Need histograms with 1s resolution during microburst to confirm anti-synchronization (not just aggregate p99).
- Add server-side queue occupancy traces and serving-runtime concurrency per-model-worker during burst to observe collision points.
- Capture retry timestamps (client-proxy) to compute inter-retry distribution and measure spacing.

Quick next experiments (prioritized):
- Repeat with longer microburst (2s), see if jitter still helps or just delays cascade.
- Try adaptive stochastic where jitter range increases proportionally to recent 1s error rate. Evaluate stability.
- Run on Dedicated-like cluster with mixed tenants (background low-priority load) to see cross-tenant coupling.

Possible production approach (tentative):
- Implement small randomized multiplicative jitter in proxy (configurable range U(0.6,1.4)) with base backoff=50ms, cap=800ms.
- Rollout can be soft (only for retries beyond 1st) and gated by traffic type (short inference jobs first).
- Add telemetry flagging: if p99 over rolling 1m > threshold, increase jitter range automatically (conservative control loop).

Open questions / risks:
- Randomized backoff trades added per-request delay for lower tail; do SLAs for short synchronous calls accept that p50/p95 shift? Need product input.
- Interactions with gateway-level rate-limiting and our prefix-kv caching (might exacerbate cold cache penalty when delaying).
- Edge cases: if retries are expensive (long generator runs), adding jitter could multiply cost. Need cost model check.

TODOs (short list):
- [ ] Instrument retry timestamps & per-replica concurrency in next run (Ravi)
- [ ] Add 1s-res histograms to bench harness (Nora)
- [ ] Try adaptive jitter policy sim (me)
- [ ] Draft short one-pager for product to discuss p50 tradeoffs once we have 2-3 more runs

Raw artifacts location:
- Local bench harness: git@github.com:redwood-inference/bench-harness (branch: stochastic-backoff/inga)
- Capture snapshots in /tmp/inga-bench-20250214.tar.gz (uploaded to S3: s3://redwood-internal/bench/inga/20250214.tgz)

Notes-to-self:
- Watch out for measurement noise — replicate each cell at least 6x and use median-of-reps for heatmap cell, not mean.
- For quick demos, show p99 reduction % vs baseline rather than absolute ms to normalize across model sizes.

End of scratchpad.
